newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN IPOs - Bleak vista stretches ahead says Prime.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN IPOs - Bleak vista stretches ahead says Prime.

text.p: The Indian IPO scenario has been dull, with just one premium issue since November, Prime Database, the country's premier primary capital market database, said on Wednesday.

"January was also a month of only par issues, even worse than the previous month which had seen one premium issue but similar to November which also had only par issues," Prithvi Haldea of Prime said in a statement.
The solitary premium issue has been that of the Bank of Baroda, he added.

Haldea said it would be a few months before the impact of the rising Sensex is felt by the primary market because of the time it requires to make a public issue, given the various SEBI and ROC regulations.
"The secondary market, in fact, will need to show significant improvements in the cash scrips before the investors even start looking back at the new issue market," Haldea said.
Substantial losses in earlier premium issues, without an exit route for over 2 years now, have left investors apathetic to premium issues.

Little wonder such issues have been declining over the past several months; only 82 issues have been at a premium in the first 10 months of the current fiscal, compared to 199 during the financial year 1993-94 (April/March), 453 in 1994-95 and 302 in 1995-96.
The number of public issues in January decreased to 34, against 38 in December, and even this number largely represented finance and 'technical' issues.

In the period from April to September, as many as 577 public issues hit the market, or an average of 96 issues per month. The first major drop was in October which had only 41, followed by 24 in November.
The manufacturing sector continued to suffer. According to Prime, just 12 percent of the total 9.01 billion rupees raised in the month, was mobilised by the manufacturing sector.
The rest was raised by the finance sector which continued to sway the market cornering 88 percent of the amount.

The dominance of the finance sector by numbers, too, continued; 17 of the 34 issues (50 percent) were from this sector. This was similar to 51 percent in December but higher than the 33 to 40 percent in the period from August to November period and 26 to 29 percent in the period April to July.
Moreover, small issues continued to dominate the market in January too; 14 of the 34 issues (41 percent) were below 30 million rupees.

Amounts in earlier months, including the retention of oversubscriptions, were 4.74 billion rupees in November, 3.16 billion rupees in October, 13.99 billion rupees in September, 3.48 billion rupees in August, 16.74 billion rupees in July, 6.84 billion rupees in June, 12.75 billion rupees in May and 3.83 billion rupees in April, according to Prime.

There continued to be an extremely poor response to issues in January. Several issues had to stay open till the last closing date. Among these were Sree Rayalaseema Power, Krimy Biscuits, Janvi Finstock, PHF Leasing and Loggar Finance.
However, the IDBI Flexibond issue managed to obtain a significant oversubscription, an indicator that investors are moving away from equity to debt.

Worse, faced with poor market conditions, 14 issues of the month did not even provide for an earliest closing date, these being Flare Finance (India), Gazi Securities, Harsha capital Services, Industrial Development Bank of India, Mardia Global Finvest, Marvel Hi-Tech, Nemox Drugs & Pharmaceuticals, Nivedan Fin-Invest-Lease, Parekh Aluminex, Parnami Habitat Developers, Raideep Industries, Sita Bhagwat Investment & Finance, Vaishali Graphics and Welspun Stahl Rohren.

During the month, the issue of Magic Touch Infotech had to be withdrawn on the eve of the opening of the subscription list. This brought to 25 the total number of issues since April which have been cancelled/withdrawn at the last moment.
According to Haldea, the private sector appears worst-hit in the present scenario with no major issues on the horizon.
The public sector will continue to dominate the market, Haldea said.

February will see the 6.75 billion-rupee equity issue of the Bank of India, and in March the ICICI 7.5-billion-rupee bond issue is expected to hit the market. Other mega offerings expected in the current fiscal, those from Canara Bank (10,000 million rupees) and Corporation Bank (2,500 million rupees), have been postponed to the next fiscal.
